operation: Local extraction of native fresh Foldseek alignment
native_database_snapshot: Not established by this extraction; retain native settings and output.log.
method: Read deposited PDB ATOM C-alpha residue identities in file order. Require unique chain-A author residue keys and no alternate locations/multiple models. Verify complete native qseq/tseq equality to independently parsed source residue sequences. Remove existing alignment gap characters only to verify native inclusive subsequence bounds, then preserve qaln/taln unchanged. Walk each alignment column and look up its original author identity by native sequence position. No residue-number offset was assumed.

numbering_convention.author_residues: PDB author chain, residue number, insertion code; preserved through explicit lookup
numbering_convention.gaps: Hyphen in alignment; blank sequence/author fields in correspondence table

identity_reporting.note: Preserve the service fident value verbatim. It is less precise than the direct integer-count fraction; do not substitute the paired-column denominator or the historical US-align identity.

limitations: This is a newly returned Foldseek alignment, not recovered historical US-align or historical Foldseek output.
No alignment, fit, coordinate transformation, geometric measurement, or structure prediction was performed during extraction.
Exact sequence identity establishes the target residue-number mapping to deposited chain A; this does not verify the target assembly operator or its coordinate orientation.
The local alignment excludes query residues outside A205-402 and mouse observed residues outside A133-328; it is not a full-length global alignment.
A 172-pair count coincides numerically with a historical US-align count but does not establish identical correspondences.
The FASTA itself has alignment-column positions; retain the correspondence TSV for original author residue numbering.
